objectives: Recall Python basics: input, print and variables.
Run and step through a program in Thonny.
Describe this term's focus: decisions and loops.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Baseline WPM run, posture check.

plan.title: Python recap
plan.detail: Work the recap worksheet: print(), input(), variables, int() conversion. The int(input()) pattern is the one they always forget - drill it now.

plan.title: Thonny tour
plan.detail: Editor, shell, variables pane. Run a short program, then run it again with the Debug button stepping line by line while watching the variables pane.

plan.title: Predict and check
plan.detail: Given three short programs, predict the output before running. Step through to see exactly where predictions were wrong.

plan.title: Term map
plan.detail: Theme: 'Python - Decisions & Loops'. Preview the mini-app project and the deadline weeks. Log out.

successCriteria: I can write a program that takes input and prints a result.
I stepped through a program watching variables change.
I know what the term project will be.

objectives: Use if, elif and else to handle several cases.
Order conditions correctly.
Build a grade-band feedback program.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why elif
plan.detail: Show four separate ifs versus if/elif/else. With separate ifs, several branches can run. Demo the bug before teaching the fix.

plan.title: Grade bands
plan.detail: Build: input a score, then fail under 40, pass 40-59, merit 60-79, distinction 80+. Watch for the classic bug: checking >40 before >80.

plan.title: Boundary testing
plan.detail: Test 39, 40, 59, 60, 79, 80. Boundaries are where the bugs live - make this a habit now, it pays off in Week 5.

plan.title: Peer swap
plan.detail: Run a partner's program with the boundary values and report any that behave wrongly. Log out.

successCriteria: My program uses if, elif and else.
Only one branch runs for any input.
My program gives the right answer at every boundary.

objectives: Use a for loop with range().
Use a while loop with a condition.
Explain when each type of loop is the right choice.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Counted vs conditional
plan.detail: for = I know how many times. while = I keep going until something changes. Real examples: 10 press-ups vs run until the bell.

plan.title: range() in detail
plan.detail: range(5), range(1,6), range(10,0,-1). Print each to see exactly what it produces - the off-by-one confusion is best resolved by looking.

plan.title: Countdown to blast-off
plan.detail: Write the countdown with a for loop, then rewrite it with a while loop. Same output, two approaches. Add a sleep for effect.

plan.title: Infinite loop
plan.detail: Deliberately write one, watch it run, stop it with the red button. Discuss what was missing. Log out.

successCriteria: I wrote a working for loop with range().
I wrote a while loop that ends correctly.
I can say which loop suits a given problem.

objectives: Combine conditions with and, or and not.
Complete a truth table.
Build a program with a two-part entry rule.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Truth tables
plan.detail: Complete the handout for and, or, not. Key point: 'and' needs both true, 'or' needs at least one.

plan.title: Rollercoaster rules
plan.detail: Build: age >= 12 and height >= 140 to ride. Then a second version with or, and compare who gets in. The difference makes the operators concrete.

plan.title: not and negation
plan.detail: Rewrite a condition using not. Discuss which version reads more clearly - clarity is a real programming judgement.

plan.title: Test the rules
plan.detail: Test values that pass both, fail both and pass only one. Log out.

successCriteria: My program combines two conditions correctly.
I tested a case that passes one condition but not the other.
I can complete a truth table for and, or and not.

objectives: Write a test plan before writing code.
Choose normal, boundary and invalid test data.
Record expected versus actual results.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Three kinds of test data
plan.detail: Normal (typical use), boundary (edges), invalid (should be rejected). Model with an age-entry program: 25, 12, -3, 'banana'.

plan.title: Write the plan first
plan.detail: Using the 3-column template, write six test cases for a program that has NOT been built yet. Planning before coding is the point of the lesson.

plan.title: Build and test
plan.detail: Build the program, then run every test case and fill in the Actual column. Any mismatch gets investigated.

plan.title: What did the plan catch?
plan.detail: Share bugs found only because the test plan existed. Log out.

activities: Write a test plan before coding
Run tests and record actual results
successCriteria: My test plan has normal, boundary and invalid cases.
I wrote the plan before the code.
I recorded actual results and investigated mismatches.

objectives: Build a number guessing game with a while loop.
Give higher/lower feedback using if and elif.
Use a random number correctly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Break down the problem
plan.detail: Decompose on the board: pick a secret number, ask, compare, respond, repeat until correct. Write the steps before any code.

plan.title: Build it
plan.detail: import random, randint(1,100), while guess != secret, if/elif for higher/lower. Support: a starter file with the loop skeleton for those who need it.

plan.title: Test with strategy
plan.detail: Play using binary search - always guess the middle. How many guesses should it take at most? A nice link to computational thinking.

plan.title: Extension
plan.detail: Count and display the number of guesses used. Save the file with a clear name. Log out.

successCriteria: My game picks a random secret number.
It gives correct higher/lower feedback.
The loop ends when the guess is correct.

objectives: Port a program from a computer to a physical device.
Adapt a design to hardware limits.
Compare MakeCode Python with desktop Python.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What has to change
plan.detail: The micro:bit has no keyboard and a 5x5 display. Discuss: how do you input a guess? How do you show higher/lower? Design constraints drive the redesign.

plan.title: Build the 1-10 version
plan.detail: Buttons increment the guess, A+B submits, arrow icons show higher/lower. Toggle to Python view and read the generated code.

plan.title: Compare the two
plan.detail: Side by side: desktop Python versus MakeCode Python. Same logic, different input and output.

plan.title: Demo
plan.detail: Swap devices and play a partner's version. Devices counted in. Log out.

successCriteria: My micro:bit version works with button input.
It shows higher/lower feedback on the display.
I can name two things the port forced me to change.

objectives: Read a Python error message and locate the fault.
Use Thonny's debugger to step through code.
Fix three broken programs systematically.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Reading errors
plan.detail: Anatomy of a traceback: the line number, the error type, the message. Cover NameError, TypeError, IndentationError and SyntaxError with an example of each.

plan.title: Debug three programs
plan.detail: Ten minutes each. Method: read the error, go to the line, step through with the debugger, form a hypothesis, change ONE thing, re-run.

plan.title: Bug taxonomy
plan.detail: Classify each bug: syntax, logic or runtime. Logic errors are the ones with no error message - the hardest kind.

plan.title: Share the trickiest
plan.detail: Which bug hid best, and what gave it away? Log out.

successCriteria: I can name the line and error type from a traceback.
I used the debugger to watch variables change.
I fixed at least two of the three programs.

resources.label: How to read a Python error - guide

objectives: Add input validation to my program.
Add a play-again loop.
Track a score across rounds.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Never trust the user
plan.detail: What happens when someone types 'banana' into a number input? Crash. Introduce validation with a while loop and .isdigit() or try/except.

plan.title: Validate and loop
plan.detail: Add: reject anything not a number 1-100, and a play-again prompt that restarts the game while the answer is yes.

plan.title: Score counter
plan.detail: Add a variable counting games played and best number of guesses. Display it at the end.

plan.title: Break it
plan.detail: Swap with a partner and try to crash their program. Report anything that breaks. Log out.

activities: Input validation with a while loop
successCriteria: My program does not crash on invalid input.
The user can play again without restarting.
A score or best result is tracked and displayed.

objectives: Write a test plan for someone else's program.
Find and fix bugs under time pressure.
Refactor code to make it clearer.

plan.title: Station briefing
plan.detail: Three stations, 20 minutes each, exam-style tasks at every station.

plan.title: Station 1 - Write a test plan
plan.detail: For a partner's program: six test cases covering normal, boundary and invalid input.

plan.title: Station 2 - Find and fix
plan.detail: Two broken exam-style programs. Diagnose in writing, then fix.

plan.title: Station 3 - Refactor
plan.detail: Take working but messy code and improve it: better variable names, comments, remove repetition. Behaviour must not change.

plan.title: Exam readiness
plan.detail: Self-rate confidence on each skill; note the weakest for revision. Log out.

activities: Write a test plan for a peer's code
successCriteria: My test plan covers all three data types.
I diagnosed bugs in writing before fixing.
My refactored code behaves identically but reads better.

objectives: Build a Python mini-app that meets a written brief.
Pass my own written test plan.
Show one bug found and fixed.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Read the brief twice. Requirements on the board: meets the brief, has a test plan, evidence of one bug found and fixed.

plan.title: Test plan first
plan.detail: Write the test plan before coding. This is assessed - remind them it carries marks even if the code is incomplete.

plan.title: Build
plan.detail: Silent conditions, technical help only. Circulate and note who is testing as they go.

plan.title: Test and evidence
plan.detail: Run every test case, fill in Actual, and screenshot the bug and its fix.

plan.title: Save and submit
plan.detail: The .py file plus the test plan into the assessment folder, correctly named.

activities: Test plan and evidence of debugging
successCriteria: My program does what the brief asks.
My test plan is complete with actual results.
I evidenced one bug found and fixed.
Both files are submitted correctly.

objectives: Choose a project and write a clear plan.
State the inputs and outputs.
Write three test cases before coding.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: The project menu
plan.detail: Quiz app, times-tables trainer, tip calculator, password strength checker. Discuss what makes each one hard - steer confident coders to the password checker.

plan.title: Plan it
plan.detail: Planning template: purpose, user, inputs, outputs, variables, the loop, the decisions.

plan.title: Three test cases
plan.detail: Write them now, before any code exists. Normal, boundary, invalid.

plan.title: Plan review
plan.detail: Teacher signs off each plan before coding starts next week. Log out.

activities: Write three test cases up front
successCriteria: My plan states the purpose, inputs and outputs.
I have identified the variables and the loop I need.
My three test cases are written before any code.

objectives: Build my mini-app from the plan.
Use variables, a loop and a condition.
Run my own test plan against it.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build order
plan.detail: Get input working, then the core logic, then the loop, then the polish. Run the program after every small addition.

plan.title: Build
plan.detail: Independent build. Circulate with targeted questions rather than solutions: 'what did you expect that line to do?'

plan.title: Self-test
plan.detail: Run the three test cases and record the actual results. Fix anything that fails. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My program uses variables, a loop and a condition.
It does the main job in the plan.
I ran all three test cases and recorded the results.

objectives: Test a partner's program using their test plan.
Add one new test case they missed.
Fix bugs and log them in a bug diary.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Peer testing
plan.detail: Swap machines. Run their test plan exactly as written, record actual results, then add one test case they missed.

plan.title: Fix the bugs
plan.detail: Back to your own code. Fix what the peer test exposed. Log each bug: what happened, why, what you changed.

plan.title: Re-test
plan.detail: Re-run the full test plan including the new case. All should pass.

plan.title: Bug of the week
plan.detail: Share the most interesting bug and its cause. Log out.

activities: Peer testing against a written plan
successCriteria: I tested a partner's program properly and recorded results.
I added one test case they had missed.
My bug diary records what happened, why, and the fix.

objectives: Demo my mini-app in three minutes.
Run my test cases live.
Explain the key parts of my code.

plan.title: Rehearse
plan.detail: Structure: what it does, live demo, run the test cases, explain the tricky part of the code.

plan.title: Demo day
plan.detail: Three minutes each. Running the test cases live is the distinctive part - it shows the app handles bad input as well as good.

plan.title: Audience questions
plan.detail: One question per presenter: 'What would you add next?', 'What was your hardest bug?'

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Final .py file plus the test plan and bug diary into the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Term reflection
plan.detail: Name the debugging habit you will keep. Log out.

activities: Run test cases in front of the class
successCriteria: I demoed within three minutes.
I ran my test cases live, including an invalid input.
My .py file and test plan are in the portfolio folder.
